column1: # The census of what bin/safedeps, lib/*.sh and lib/*/*.sh hand a command as
# an argument: scripts/test/argv-census.sh holds the code to it, both ways,
# with scripts/test/lib/argv-census.py, which says what each column means.
# The rule: a file's contents, or a value whose length nothing bounds, reaches
# a command through a file, standard input or a pipe, never as an argument or
# in the environment. macOS counts the arguments and the environment together
# against ARG_MAX; Linux refuses one string longer than MAX_ARG_STRLEN. Shell
# builtins, shell functions, here-strings and pipes are not bounded that way.
# A new jq value argument, or one whose count moved, is a mismatch until a row
# here names it with its class and why. `argv-census.py list --root .` prints
# the forms as the check reads them. A follow-up row is a place the rule does
# not hold yet; the change that takes it is named in its why. The environment
# carries no file contents in this scope: its exports and prefix assignments
